CVE-2025-67746.title: Composer is a dependency manager for PHP. In versions on the 2.x  ...
CVE-2025-67746.description: Composer is a dependency manager for PHP. In versions on the 2.x branch prior to 2.2.26 and 2.9.3, attackers controlling remote sources that Composer downloads from might in some way inject ANSI control characters in the terminal output of various Composer commands, causing mangled output and potentially leading to confusion or DoS of the terminal application. There is no proven exploit and this has thus a low severity but we still publish a CVE as it has potential for abuse, and we want to be on the safe side informing users that they should upgrade. Versions 2.2.26 and 2.9.3 contain a patch for the issue.

CVE-2026-40176.title: Composer is a dependency manager for PHP. Versions 1.0 through 2. ...
CVE-2026-40176.description: Composer is a dependency manager for PHP. Versions 1.0 through 2.2.26 and 2.3 through 2.9.5 contain a command injection vulnerability in the Perforce::generateP4Command() method, which constructs shell commands by interpolating user-supplied Perforce connection parameters (port, user, client) without proper escaping. An attacker can inject arbitrary commands through these values in a malicious composer.json declaring a Perforce VCS repository, leading to command execution in the context of the user running Composer, even if Perforce is not installed. VCS repositories are only loaded from the root composer.json or the composer config directory, so this cannot be exploited through composer.json files of packages installed as dependencies. Users are at risk if they run Composer commands on untrusted projects with attacker-supplied composer.json files. This issue has been fixed in Composer 2.2.27 (2.2 LTS) and 2.9.6 (mainline).

CVE-2026-40261.title: Composer is a dependency manager for PHP. Versions 1.0 through 2. ...
CVE-2026-40261.description: Composer is a dependency manager for PHP. Versions 1.0 through 2.2.26 and 2.3 through 2.9.5 contain a command injection vulnerability in the Perforce::syncCodeBase() method, which appends the $sourceReference parameter to a shell command without proper escaping, and additionally in the Perforce::generateP4Command() method as in GHSA-wg36-wvj6-r67p / CVE-2026-40176, which interpolates user-supplied Perforce connection parameters (port, user, client) from the source url field without proper escaping. An attacker can inject arbitrary commands through crafted source reference or source url values containing shell metacharacters, even if Perforce is not installed. Unlike CVE-2026-40176, the source reference and url are provided as part of package metadata, meaning any compromised or malicious Composer repository can serve package metadata declaring perforce as a source type with malicious values. This vulnerability is exploitable when installing or updating dependencies from source, including the default behavior when installing dev-prefixed versions. This issue has been fixed in Composer 2.2.27 (2.2 LTS) and 2.9.6 (mainline). If developers are unable to immediately update, they can avoid installing dependencies from source by using --prefer-dist or the preferred-install: dist config setting, and only use trusted Composer repositories as a workaround.

CVE-2026-45793.title: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. Prior to 1 ...
CVE-2026-45793.description: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. Prior to 1.10.28, 2.2.28, and 2.9.8, Composer\IO\BaseIO::loadConfiguration() validates GitHub OAuth tokens with the regex ^[.A-Za-z0-9_]+$ and interpolates rejected tokens into an UnexpectedValueException; GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN values using the ghs_<id>_<base64url-JWT> format can contain -, fail validation, and be disclosed to stderr or CI logs. This issue is fixed in versions 1.10.28, 2.2.28, and 2.9.8.

CVE-2026-59944.title: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. From 1.0 u ...
CVE-2026-59944.description: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. From 1.0 until 2.2.30 and from 2.3.0 until 2.10.3, a malicious or compromised dependency can bypass the earlier CVE-2026-59946 binary-path hardening because Composer validates literal parent-directory segments only during dependency resolution, while the symlink and installed-metadata paths described by the advisory skip that validation. A package can ship an in-package binary symlink that resolves outside its installation directory, or attacker-influenced vendor/composer/installed.json metadata can provide an escaping binary path during a reinstall or regeneration of missing vendor/bin entries. The installed-metadata path is reachable only when the vendor directory was not populated by the same validated install run, such as when it is restored from an untrusted cache, copied from an earlier build stage, carried over from an older Composer run, or writable by a lower-trust build step. Composer can follow the path, change the external target's permissions to make it world-readable and executable, and create a runnable vendor/bin proxy to that external file. The issue does not directly read or transmit data and does not by itself provide remote code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.30 and 2.10.3.

CVE-2026-59946.title: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. Prior to 2 ...
CVE-2026-59946.description: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. Prior to 2.2.29 and 2.10.2, a Composer package bin entry containing .. path segments can resolve outside the package install directory and cause Composer's binary installation flow to chmod an existing host file to a world-readable and world-executable mode during composer install, update, or require. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.29 and 2.10.2.

CVE-2026-59947.title: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. Prior to 2 ...
CVE-2026-59947.description: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. Prior to 2.2.29 and 2.10.2, when Composer is run with -vvv debug verbosity, it could print a credential embedded in the username slot of a repository or package URL, such as a GitHub Personal Access Token in https://TOKEN@host/, to debug output because AuthHelper, Url::sanitize, and ProcessExecutor did not sanitize username-only URL credentials. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.29 and 2.10.2.

CVE-2026-59948.title: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. Prior to 2 ...
CVE-2026-59948.description: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. Prior to 2.2.29 and 2.10.2, a maliciously crafted package from an untrusted repository other than Packagist.org or Private Packagist can cause Composer to write attacker-controlled files outside the vendor directory and outside the project during install or update by using an invalid package name that is not correctly validated before dependency-resolution results are written or installed. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.29 and 2.10.2.

CVE-2026-84361.title: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. From 1.0 u ...
CVE-2026-84361.description: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. From 1.0 until 2.2.30 and 2.10.3, a malicious dependency package from a custom Composer repository or an untrusted composer.lock file could set source.type to perforce and source.url to an rsh: or jsh: P4PORT value. When the Perforce p4 client was installed and Composer installed the package from source through composer install or composer update, including --prefer-source, Composer\Util\Perforce passed the address to p4 without validation, causing p4 to run a local command with the privileges of the user or CI account. Packagist.org does not permit Perforce source metadata. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.30 and 2.10.3.

GHSA-jhfp-4ppm-crmm.title: Arbitrary command execution via `transport-options.prevent_url_access_callable` loaded from `composer.lock` / `installed.json`
GHSA-jhfp-4ppm-crmm.description: ## Summary A crafted `composer.lock` or `vendor/composer/installed.json` could cause Composer to run an arbitrary system command while resolving downloads during `composer install` or `composer update`. This is data-driven arbitrary command execution: it does not require a malicious package to be installed or any package code to run, only the ability to influence those two files, and the command runs before any checksum or integrity check. It is not a flaw in how trusted package code executes. ## Am I affected? You are affected if all of the following hold: - You run Composer 2.10.0 through 2.11.1. - You run `composer install` or `composer update` against a `composer.lock` or `vendor/composer/installed.json` whose contents an attacker could influence. Realistic ways that file becomes attacker-influenced include a pull request that only edits `composer.lock`, a shared or scaffolded project template that ships a lock file, a compromised dependency-update bot, or a CI cache that restores a poisoned lock or installed file. You are plainly not affected if nothing untrusted can modify your lock or installed-packages files, or if you are on the 2.2 LTS line (or any release before 2.10.0), which never had the affected option handling. The single most realistic way to get hit: automated CI that checks out a branch and runs `composer install` without a human reviewing the lock-file change. `--no-scripts` and `--no-plugins` do not prevent it. ## Patched versions Fixed in 2.11.2. The fix makes Composer ignore these download-time callback options when they come from the lock or installed-packages file, and only honor them when they are set programmatically. ## Workarounds The only complete fix is upgrading. To reduce risk until then, do not run `composer install`/`update` on lock or installed files from untrusted sources (unreviewed pull requests outside of CI running sandboxed, third-party templates, shared caches).

GHSA-w6hj-6587-3jh5.title: Arbitrary file write outside the package directory via symlinked zip entries and the `unzip` to `ZipArchive` extraction fallback
GHSA-w6hj-6587-3jh5.description: ## Summary A malicious package archive could cause Composer to write a file outside the intended package directory during `composer install`, `composer update`, or `composer require`. Because the written file can be an application entry point or another file that later gets executed, this can lead to code execution. It is arbitrary file write, not a flaw triggered by normal Packagist-hosted packages, which do not carry the kind of archive entries required. ## Am I affected? You are affected if all of the following hold: - You run Composer 1.0.0 through 2.11.1. - You install packages whose distribution archive (zip) an attacker can control. In practice this means untrusted third-party Composer repositories, private or self-hosted repositories, artifact mirrors, or any attacker-controlled dist URL. - Your system has the `unzip` command available (standard on Linux and macOS) together with the PHP zip extension. When those hold, a crafted archive can redirect one of its entries so the content lands outside the package directory, for example overwriting a front controller in the project root, which yields code execution on the next request or command. You are plainly not affected if every package you install comes from a trusted source. Packagist.org-hosted archives generally do not contain the archive entries this relies on, so typical Packagist.org-only installs are not a realistic vector. The single most realistic way to get hit: adding or updating a package served by an untrusted or attacker-controlled repository or mirror. ## Patched versions Fixed in 2.11.2 and 2.2.32. ## Workarounds The only complete fix is upgrading.

GHSA-x82q-x274-r6pq.title: Inline repository HTTP credentials sent to attacker controlled dist mirrors supplied in `composer.lock` / `installed.json`
GHSA-x82q-x274-r6pq.description: ## Summary For projects that authenticate to a Composer repository using an inline HTTP header credential, a crafted `composer.lock` or `vendor/composer/installed.json` could cause that credential to be sent to a download mirror on an attacker-controlled host during `composer install`. This is an information disclosure issue limited to that repository credential. There is no code execution and no file modification. ## Am I affected? You are affected if all of the following hold: - You run Composer 2.11.0, 2.11.1, or 2.2.31. - You configure a Composer repository with an inline HTTP header that carries a secret, for example an `Authorization` bearer token or an API key set in the repository's options (common with Private Packagist and Satis-style setups). - An attacker can influence your `composer.lock` or `vendor/composer/installed.json`, for example through a pull request that edits the lock file, a committed lock in a shared project, or a poisoned CI cache. When those hold, a crafted entry can add a preferred download mirror pointing at a host the attacker controls, and the repository credential is then sent to that host. You are plainly not affected if your repositories do not use an inline header credential, or if you are on a release that does not re-attach repository headers at load time (any version other than 2.11.0, 2.11.1, and 2.2.31). ## Patched versions Fixed in 2.11.2 and 2.2.32. ## Workarounds The only complete fix is upgrading.

Prior to 2.2.29 and 2.10.2, a Composer package bin entry containing .. path segments can resolve outside the package install directory and cause Composer's binary installation flow to chmod an existing host file to a world-readable and world-executable mode during composer install, update, or require. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.29 and 2.10.2.

CVE-2026-59947.title: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. Prior to 2 ...
CVE-2026-59947.description: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. Prior to 2.2.29 and 2.10.2, when Composer is run with -vvv debug verbosity, it could print a credential embedded in the username slot of a repository or package URL, such as a GitHub Personal Access Token in https://TOKEN@host/, to debug output because AuthHelper, Url::sanitize, and ProcessExecutor did not sanitize username-only URL credentials. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.29 and 2.10.2.

CVE-2026-59948.title: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. Prior to 2 ...
CVE-2026-59948.description: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. Prior to 2.2.29 and 2.10.2, a maliciously crafted package from an untrusted repository other than Packagist.org or Private Packagist can cause Composer to write attacker-controlled files outside the vendor directory and outside the project during install or update by using an invalid package name that is not correctly validated before dependency-resolution results are written or installed. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.29 and 2.10.2.

CVE-2026-84361.description: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. From 1.0 until 2.2.30 and 2.10.3, a malicious dependency package from a custom Composer repository or an untrusted composer.lock file could set source.type to perforce and source.url to an rsh: or jsh: P4PORT value. When the Perforce p4 client was installed and Composer installed the package from source through composer install or composer update, including --prefer-source, Composer\Util\Perforce passed the address to p4 without validation, causing p4 to run a local command with the privileges of the user or CI account. Packagist.org does not permit Perforce source metadata. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.30 and 2.10.3.

GHSA-jhfp-4ppm-crmm.title: Arbitrary command execution via `transport-options.prevent_url_access_callable` loaded from `composer.lock` / `installed.json`
GHSA-jhfp-4ppm-crmm.description: ## Summary A crafted `composer.lock` or `vendor/composer/installed.json` could cause Composer to run an arbitrary system command while resolving downloads during `composer install` or `composer update`. This is data-driven arbitrary command execution: it does not require a malicious package to be installed or any package code to run, only the ability to influence those two files, and the command runs before any checksum or integrity check. It is not a flaw in how trusted package code executes. ## Am I affected? You are affected if all of the following hold: - You run Composer 2.10.0 through 2.11.1. - You run `composer install` or `composer update` against a `composer.lock` or `vendor/composer/installed.json` whose contents an attacker could influence. Realistic ways that file becomes attacker-influenced include a pull request that only edits `composer.lock`, a shared or scaffolded project template that ships a lock file, a compromised dependency-update bot, or a CI cache that restores a poisoned lock or installed file. You are plainly not affected if nothing untrusted can modify your lock or installed-packages files, or if you are on the 2.2 LTS line (or any release before 2.10.0), which never had the affected option handling. The single most realistic way to get hit: automated CI that checks out a branch and runs `composer install` without a human reviewing the lock-file change. `--no-scripts` and `--no-plugins` do not prevent it. ## Patched versions Fixed in 2.11.2. The fix makes Composer ignore these download-time callback options when they come from the lock or installed-packages file, and only honor them when they are set programmatically. ## Workarounds The only complete fix is upgrading. To reduce risk until then, do not run `composer install`/`update` on lock or installed files from untrusted sources (unreviewed pull requests outside of CI running sandboxed, third-party templates, shared caches).

GHSA-w6hj-6587-3jh5.title: Arbitrary file write outside the package directory via symlinked zip entries and the `unzip` to `ZipArchive` extraction fallback
GHSA-w6hj-6587-3jh5.description: ## Summary A malicious package archive could cause Composer to write a file outside the intended package directory during `composer install`, `composer update`, or `composer require`. Because the written file can be an application entry point or another file that later gets executed, this can lead to code execution. It is arbitrary file write, not a flaw triggered by normal Packagist-hosted packages, which do not carry the kind of archive entries required. ## Am I affected? You are affected if all of the following hold: - You run Composer 1.0.0 through 2.11.1. - You install packages whose distribution archive (zip) an attacker can control. In practice this means untrusted third-party Composer repositories, private or self-hosted repositories, artifact mirrors, or any attacker-controlled dist URL. - Your system has the `unzip` command available (standard on Linux and macOS) together with the PHP zip extension. When those hold, a crafted archive can redirect one of its entries so the content lands outside the package directory, for example overwriting a front controller in the project root, which yields code execution on the next request or command. You are plainly not affected if every package you install comes from a trusted source. Packagist.org-hosted archives generally do not contain the archive entries this relies on, so typical Packagist.org-only installs are not a realistic vector. The single most realistic way to get hit: adding or updating a package served by an untrusted or attacker-controlled repository or mirror. ## Patched versions Fixed in 2.11.2 and 2.2.32. ## Workarounds The only complete fix is upgrading.

GHSA-x82q-x274-r6pq.title: Inline repository HTTP credentials sent to attacker controlled dist mirrors supplied in `composer.lock` / `installed.json`
GHSA-x82q-x274-r6pq.description: ## Summary For projects that authenticate to a Composer repository using an inline HTTP header credential, a crafted `composer.lock` or `vendor/composer/installed.json` could cause that credential to be sent to a download mirror on an attacker-controlled host during `composer install`. This is an information disclosure issue limited to that repository credential. There is no code execution and no file modification. ## Am I affected? You are affected if all of the following hold: - You run Composer 2.11.0, 2.11.1, or 2.2.31. - You configure a Composer repository with an inline HTTP header that carries a secret, for example an `Authorization` bearer token or an API key set in the repository's options (common with Private Packagist and Satis-style setups). - An attacker can influence your `composer.lock` or `vendor/composer/installed.json`, for example through a pull request that edits the lock file, a committed lock in a shared project, or a poisoned CI cache. When those hold, a crafted entry can add a preferred download mirror pointing at a host the attacker controls, and the repository credential is then sent to that host. You are plainly not affected if your repositories do not use an inline header credential, or if you are on a release that does not re-attach repository headers at load time (any version other than 2.11.0, 2.11.1, and 2.2.31). ## Patched versions Fixed in 2.11.2 and 2.2.32. ## Workarounds The only complete fix is upgrading.
